summary: High P99 latency spikes after region-pin rotation for enterprise customer in ch-central: multi-hop routing oscillation
description: Issue summary: LumaHealth reports persistent P99 spikes (2–6s) for inference requests from ch-central after they rotated their region-pin TTL and triggered a pin refresh. Impact: customer-facing production endpoints for patient triage are experiencing degraded tail latency and occasional streaming disconnects. Timeline: 2026-03-11 22:10 UTC pin rotation initiated by customer via Console; 2026-03-11 22:12–22:40 UTC intermittent P99 spikes observed and escalated to Support. Environment: prod traffic routed through Hosted API into Dedicated pool reserved for LumaHealth, tenant set to enterprise with strict data residency to ch-central. Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a request from ch-central region with model redwood-vicuna-13b pinned to ch-central. 2) Adjust the pin TTL via Console to force a pin rotation. 3) Send steady load (RPS ~20) and monitor p50/p95/p99 on Console route and on Grafana. Observed behavior: After pin rotation we see routing decisions oscillate between direct ch-central serving nodes and fallback paths that route through eu-west-1 and occasionally us-central-1, adding extra network hops and TLS handshakes. This correlates with p99 spikes and occasional stream resets. Expected behavior: Pin rotation should preserve residency with sticky routing to local serving nodes or, if fallback occurs, a single consistent fallback path without oscillation. Attachments: request traces, Console route snapshots, Grafana panels, and a short packet-trace excerpt attached in comments.
steps_to_reproduce: Initiate region-pin TTL update for an enterprise tenant pinned to ch-central via Console
Sustain steady generation load to the tenant's API key at ~20 RPS with redwood-vicuna-13b
Observe routing decisions in Console and p99 on route-level Grafana for 10 minutes
investigation_notes: Initial triage: routing logs show frequent changes in selected serving cluster within the 5m window following a pin TTL refresh.

Hypothesis A: pin refresh triggers a short-lived evaluation window that allows smart-routing policies to re-evaluate candidate regions; if health signals are marginal, it may oscillate between primary and fallback pools.
Hypothesis B: dedicated-pool autoscaler briefly reports capacity 'available' then 'throttled' as new worker nodes join which causes routing to flip to alternative regions.
SRE check: no node-wide kernel or NIC errors reported on ch-central pool; recent kernel upgrade was rolled out yesterday to a subset of eu-west but not ch-central.
Trace sample: full trace shows extra TLS handshake when routed via us-central (adds ~180–220ms), multiple KV cache misses on fallback nodes add another ~120–200ms per request.
Related: observed similar routing oscillation in INT-4021 during a canary last month when autoscaling was aggressive.
comments: Customer (2026-03-11 22:45 UTC): We're seeing P99 jump from ~700ms to 3–4s intermittently after we changed the pin TTL — this is impacting our triage flows. Can you explain why requests are leaving CH?

Support (Asha Patel, 2026-03-11 23:02 UTC): Thanks for the report. We're opening an investigation and collecting route-level traces and Grafana panels. Can you confirm if you changed any Dedicated pool scaling policies at the same time?
Customer (2026-03-11 23:10 UTC): No scaling changes. Only updated the pin TTL via Console to test faster failover behavior. We need a fix or a recommended rollback plan.

Support (Diego Martinez, 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC): Preliminary routing logs attached. We see route-select flips between ch-central and eu-west; we're engaging SRE to look for autoscaling or health-report flaps.

SRE (Marta Ivanov, 2026-03-12 10:15 UTC): Observed brief worker registration delays in ch-central between 22:10–22:16 UTC correlated with the pin rotation window. Worker join events were followed by transient 'throttled' flags from the scheduler for ~40s.

Eng (Luis Chen, 2026-03-12 13:40 UTC): Kernel configuration mismatch ruled out; we reproduced oscillation in a staging replay by toggling pin TTL and simulating delayed worker joins. Suggestion: pause smart-routing re-eval on pin-refresh for 60s to allow pool stabilization.

Support (Diego Martinez, 2026-03-14 09:20 UTC): Planned mitigation: apply a temporary routing policy to LumaHealth tenant that pins sticky routing for 90s post-pin-rotation and disable immediate canary fallback. ETA for change: 2026-03-14 11:00 UTC. Will monitor p99 for 1 hour post-change.
Customer (LumaHealth SRE, 2026-03-14 09:35 UTC): Please proceed with the mitigation. We'll hold further pin TTL changes until you confirm stabilization.
root_cause: Smart-routing re-evaluation during region-pin TTL rotation overlapped with transient dedicated-pool worker registration delays. The combination allowed the routing policy to flip between primary and remote clusters, producing multi-hop fallbacks and cache misses that increased tail latency.
resolution: Applied temporary tenant-level routing override to enforce sticky local routing for 90s after any pin-change event. Adjusted scheduler backoff to surface worker readiness earlier to the routing layer. Monitoring shows P99 returned to baseline (~650–800ms) for the customer after mitigation.
postmortem_actions: Create a policy to suppress routing re-evaluation for 60–120s after explicit pin TTL updates (ENG-4312)
Improve dedicated-pool worker readiness signals to reduce registration-to-ready window (SRE-2198)
Add a Console warning when users change pin TTL that outlines potential transient latency during worker rejoin
Follow-up with LumaHealth CS to schedule a 1:1 to review changes and confirm acceptance of mitigation
